key_insight: A tunable methylammonium polybromide melt can directly convert elemental metal films into optoelectronic-grade bromide perovskites in a single, solvent-free step at room temperature.
engineering_relevance: This enables lower-complexity, potentially roll-to-roll-compatible manufacturing of perovskite films from stable metal precursors, including difficult multivalent systems.
method: Use methylammonium polybromide melt (PBM) as the reactive medium.
React PBM directly with metal films such as Pb, Sn, Au, and Cu at room temperature.
Adjust PBM composition to control reactivity and suppress unwanted overoxidation, especially for Sn.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful conversion of Pb, Sn, Au, and Cu films into MAPbBr3, MASnBr3, MA2Au2Br6, and MA2CuBr4, with in situ XRD observing transient intermediates in two cases.
watch_item: Reaction outcomes depend on oxidation/disproportionation potentials and PBM tuning, so process windows may be metal-specific and sensitive to composition control.
paper_title: A Universal Polybromide Melt Strategy for the Direct Conversion of Metals into Optoelectronic-Grade Bromide Perovskites
